subject: nectar bat tongue
title: This Bat's Tongue Is Longer Than Its Body, So It Keeps It in Its Chest

scenes.text: This bat's tongue is longer than its whole body.
The tube-lipped nectar bat lives in the cloud forests of Ecuador. Its body is about five and a half centimeters long.
Its tongue reaches eight and a half. One and a half times its body, a record for any mammal.
A tongue that long can't fit in a mouth. So its base sits deep in the chest, inside the rib cage.
One flower hides its nectar at the bottom of a tube eight to nine centimeters deep. Only this bat pollinates it.
Science didn't even describe this bat until 2005.

description:
The tube-lipped nectar bat of Ecuador has a tongue one and a half times as long as its body.
The bat is about 5.5 cm long and its tongue reaches about 8.5 cm, the longest of any mammal relative to body size. When not in use, the tongue is drawn back into the chest, with its base inside the rib cage. The flower Centropogon nigricans, whose tube is 8 to 9 cm deep, is pollinated only by this bat. The species was described in 2005 and its tongue was reported in Nature in 2006.
Which animal has the strangest tongue?
